channels.channel: opening-group and proximity vectors, message half (the internal boundaries and the two external endpoints)
channels.how: every group of these commitments is a singleton, so at each of the 1,024 message positions the view is one 2(G+1) x (non-data rows) system over Fp; with the hidden data fixed to zero it is solved exactly and the view recomputed entry by entry

channels.how: recomputed from the exhibited zero-data randomness and compared with the capture

channels.channel: opening-group and proximity vectors of A and H
channels.reason: their opening groups have several members, so each claim's own published value is an extra constraint; the correction step that handles it is in zk60_native_pg_pcs, whose MSG == PAD == 256 does not hold at this shape (1,024 message positions against 256 pads)

what_is_computed_instead.note: A discloses 0 and H discloses 2, the public LogUp identity, with a certifying minor; that is a rank, not a preimage

channels.channel: the pad half of every published vector
channels.reason: constructing it needs the Lagrange interpolation through the distinct sampled nodes and the Z_S divisibility test of zk60_native_pg_pcs, which assumes MSG == PAD; what IS computed is H-pad, the exact rank of the pad block over the distinct opened columns

channels.channel: opened column values

channels.channel: the Merkle roots (A, H, M per stage, the L-1 boundary roots, the two endpoint roots)
channels.model_assumption: the roots are generated by the prover itself (ruling D18) and indistinguishability rests on M-2, the hiding of unopened salted leaves in the random-oracle model.  A boundary root is an observed commitment and NOT part of the run statement

channels.channel: leaf salts
channels.model_assumption: fresh uniform bytes in both worlds; equality of the two laws rests on M-3, the assumption that the whole output stream of ZkRng is indistinguishable from uniform

channels.channel: authentication paths
channels.model_assumption: the paths are genuine hashes of the same world's own columns; hiding of the unopened leaf digests rests on M-2

channels.channel: the sequencing surface: the number of segments, their byte lengths and their position tags
channels.model_assumption: L is a public word of the run statement (absorbed under run-shape) and a segment's length is a function of the shape and of the stage's position, not of the witness; the position tags are squeezed from a DISCARDED transcript clone, compared by the verifier and never absorbed (ruling M-6), so they are a public function of public transcript data.  EVIDENCE, not proof: the two bundles are independent runs on different hidden inputs and their three segment lengths agree exactly

channels.channel: the cross-block joint law beyond the linear rank
channels.reason: obligation O-R3: what is computed here is a RANK of a linear model over the run's commitments.  That the three views of a boundary plane are jointly input-free needs per-commitment independent blinding (O-R2, verified in the code, not here) and a composition argument for a run, which is unwritten.  The check's OMITTED CONDITION 7 -- that the gate must rank the two A commitments that hold the same plane, not the boundary alone -- IS met by stage 4(b)

channels.channel: the preimage construction for a RUN (one randomness reproducing the whole run's view under a fixed input)
channels.reason: exhibited here per commitment, message half only, for the 4 singleton-group commitments of the run.  A RUN preimage is a joint object: it must reproduce every stage's view at once with the boundary planes shared between three commitments, and it needs the pad half and the CFS channel first

channels.channel: the boundary scale tags and the one calibration identity
channels.reason: check A7.5: nothing in the run's privacy section covers the boundary's scale/calibration binding, and D12 item 5 records that a tag equality check would pass on a factor-of-8 mismatch.  The gate reads the scales as public constants and checks that the run declares ONE calibration identity (ruling M-4); it does not check what the tag proves

channels.channel: whether a proof attempt produced a receipt (refusal events)
channels.reason: the refusal channel is inside the game (ruling C-2); a capture exists only when the run was accepted.  For a RUN the check adds one more refusal class: with 49 commitments a run makes 23 more ZkRng::from_os calls, and from_os fails closed -- now possibly in stage 12, minutes in (A7.2)
